newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway oil investments seen rising in '97.
newsitem.headline: Norway oil investments seen rising in '97.

text.p: Total oil and gas investments on the Norwegian shelf are forecast at 51.5 billion crowns in 1997, up 6.9 billion from this year, Statistics Norway said on Thursday.
In a quarterly report on key economic indicators, the government statistics office attributed the expected increase mainly to field investments.
Those investments, which comprise developing new fields and some upgrading of old ones, are expected to rise to 27.3 billion crowns from 20.8 billion this year, a statement said.
Investment in exploration activity is expected to grow to 7.8 billion crowns from 6.4 billion this year.
"Several operators say that some of the exploration activity that was planned for the second half of this year will be moved into 1997," the statement said.
The total figure of 51.5 billion crowns also includes costs for producing oil and gas, onshore activities and pipelines.
